payload.text: A cell is placed in a solution in which the concentration of a small, nonpolar solute is higher outside the cell than inside. The solute can cross the phospholipid bilayer directly.

stimuli.alt_text: A cell in a solution where a small nonpolar solute is more concentrated outside than inside.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the solute will move into the cell, and identify whether this movement requires energy input from the cell.

criteria.description: Explains movement down the concentration gradient (from higher to lower concentration) by diffusion.
Identifies the movement as passive transport requiring no cellular energy (no ATP).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Predict how the net movement of the solute will change as its concentration inside and outside the cell become equal, and justify your prediction.

criteria.description: Predicts that net movement decreases to zero (dynamic equilibrium) as concentrations equalize.
Justifies that at equal concentrations there is no net concentration gradient, though molecules still move both directions equally.

accessibility.accommodation_notes: Text-only item with alt_text; typed-text responses.
